removal_room.name: Removal Room
removal_room.description: A synthesis shell, 5.35 m of it: three registers standing on one plinth, each holding the SAME single subtraction under a different account of what the cut left. gone is the survivors and nothing where the rule cut, which is what all six members of the `removal` family ship and the only account the mathematics endorses. ghost restores every removed cell as a pale full-size volume at alpha 0.16, so the operation becomes legible and the object becomes a lie about its own definition - at three of the four cuts the ghost register is exactly the original solid again. scar keeps neither the part nor its absence but a dark core at 0.22 of the cell where the cell used to be: a fact about the cutting rather than about either state. The cut underneath all three is computed once at build time and read three ways. Nothing here moves, nothing here is random, and the artifact has no per-frame code at all.
interactions: read the row left to right - gone, ghost, scar - and notice none of the three is the honest one
compare the same cut under three accounts of its own remainder
switch the cut and watch which account changes and which does not
removal_room.capacity: SEE that a subtraction has no preferred record: drawing nothing is true about the set and loses the operation, drawing the offcut recovers the operation and denies the definition, and drawing the wound keeps neither state
removal_room.qfep_connection: F is the cut: one rule, evaluated once in _run(), identical in all three registers, which is why the row is a comparison and not three drawings. E is the three accounts, and they are irreducible to each other - a ghost cannot be recovered from a scar and neither can be recovered from an empty cell, which is why the family needed a word for the choice at all. lambda is how much of what was removed the record is willing to carry. The dark spot is `gone`: it is the value every one of the six members ships, it is the value that looks like no decision at all, and it is the one that makes the operation unrecoverable from the object.
removal_room.relationships:
Synthesised out of the six artifacts that declare a `removal` axis - [[cantor_set]], [[example_8_4_cantor_set_vr]], [[fractal_cantor_set]], [[menger_sponge]], [[recursive_chair]], [[test_scene_3]] - every one of which is a fractal of subtraction, and one artifact from the family's border.

THE EXACT COMPLEMENT OF [[retention_corridor]]. That corridor asks what a MARK KEEPS and holds five values of `retention` standing at once while varying the pass underneath them; this room asks what a CUT LEAVES and holds three values of `removal` standing at once while varying the cut underneath them. The two artifacts are built to the same rule and refuse their family's word for the same reason - see dna.kin - and between them they cover the two halves of one question: what a system does with what it wrote, and what a system does with what it threw away.

[[cantor_set]] is the ORIGIN of the vocabulary (promoted 2026-08-03) and owns the value list. Its REMOVALS const is PRELOADED by this room rather than retyped, so the two cannot drift; if that const changes or disappears this file fails at parse time. Its `third` rule is drawn here line for line - offset = L/3, new_length = L/3, one row per level, the removed middle drawn at the CHILD's level index and not the parent's - which is why `third` is the only value whose register is a history rather than a state.

[[menger_sponge]] contributes `cross` and the precondition the whole family runs on: its 27 sub-cubes partition the parent exactly, so the complement is a real set and can be drawn at all. Its keep_positions table is read here as its complement, {4,10,12,13,14,16,22}, so the seven deleted cells are stated once rather than inferred from twenty.

[[recursive_chair]] contributes `figure` and is the one member of a family of fractals whose subtraction does NOT recurse: 27 cells, 11 deleted, once, and what is left is a named object. Its own truth line - the chair was always inside the cube, subdivision merely removed what was not chair - is the reason this room can hold a non-fractal value without leaving the family.

[[sierpinski_triangle]] is NOT a member and is declared as an import. It asks this family's exact question under a rival word - `excision`, five values, absence | ghost | rubble | cast | negative - and its medial triangle is a real disjoint complement, so `gasket` puts the two vocabularies against one cut instead of leaving them in two registries.

[[sierpinski_pyramid]] REFUSED `removal` on the record, because its five children's bounding volumes interpenetrate and there is no complement to draw. It is deliberately NOT a value here: at that cut ghost and scar would have nothing to draw and the register row would collapse to three copies of `gone`.

[[evidence_ladder]] is not a source and is quoted anyway, for its construction rule: one copy of the arithmetic, evaluated once, read N ways. _run() fills four arrays and all three registers read them; nothing on this shell re-derives a cut.

spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 5.41 m, h 1.64 m, registry.measurements)

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - the shell is boxes at known constants, so this AABB is arithmetic over SHELL_W + 2*CORNICE_OVER, the cornice head at SILL_Y+PANEL_H+LINTEL_H+CORNICE_H, and z from the cornice back (-0.645) to the plinth and CELL front (+0.50). NOT a Godot measurement pass; re-measure when one is run.

dna.default: subtraction=cross. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is no preservation duty and the default is a free design choice; it was used to pick the STRONGEST single reading rather than the emptiest. `cross` is menger_sponge's cut, and it is the one value at which all three accounts are simultaneously at full strength: the 27 cells partition the parent exactly, so gone is a solid with seven holes in it, ghost is the ORIGINAL CUBE restored to the byte, and scar is seven dark cores standing in the air inside a lattice. `third` is stronger as an argument and weaker as a photograph - a Cantor ladder is mostly empty panel - and `gasket` is an import rather than a member, which is the wrong thing to lead with. The DECLARED ORDER is cross, third, gasket, figure, because build_dna_gallery trims value lists from the TAIL: the default goes first and the rest run in descending separation from it, so a capped run drops the pair that is closest together rather than the pair that is furthest apart.
dna.was: nothing. This artifact did not exist before this pass. It is the cross-member comparison that six registry notes each described from inside one value of it, built as a body. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of every registry file returns exactly 6 entries declaring `removal`, all six with the identical value list [gone, ghost, scar].
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE ROOM MAKES, and no member can make it. Each of the six stands in ONE account and forgoes the other two, and none of them has ever had to say that it was choosing. Held side by side the three accounts are not a scale and not an ordering: `gone` is the only one the mathematics endorses and it destroys the operation, because a cell that was never made cannot be told from a cell that was never in the rule. `ghost` recovers the operation completely and is a lie about the object's own definition - at `cross`, `gasket` and `figure` the ghost register is EXACTLY the original solid, which is to say the picture of a Menger sponge with its removals marked is a picture of a cube. `scar` keeps neither state: it is the only account that is about the CUTTING, and it is the only one that would still be legible if you did not already know the rule. Legibility peaks at scar, fidelity peaks at gone, and recoverability peaks at ghost, and they are three different registers.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THAT THE FAMILY HAS TWO SCAR IMPLEMENTATIONS AND NOBODY HAS SAID SO. cantor_set and example_8_4_cantor_set_vr thin the SECTION and keep the removed part's LENGTH - box.size = Vector3(seg.y, thin, thin) - so the wound has the extent of the thing that went. menger_sponge and recursive_chair take 0.22 in all three dimensions - box.size = Vector3(thin, thin, thin) - so their wound loses the extent too. Both were copied 'value for value' from the same origin, both registries say so, and they are not the same rule: one draws where the part was and how big it was, the other draws only where. Each cut in this room gets the one its own member wrote, and the room is the first place the two have stood next to each other.

ONE CUT, EVALUATED ONCE. _run() fills _keep_p/_keep_s and _cut_p/_cut_s at build time and all three registers read those four arrays; the ghost register scales nothing and the scar register applies _scar_size to the same _cut_s. Nothing re-derives a cut, so no register can drift out of agreement with another.

THE GROUND IS COMPUTED RATHER THAN PICKED, and it is the one thing this room can do for the family without touching the family's recipes. The ghost mark is unshaded pale, Rec.709 luminance 0.881524, at alpha 0.16; the scar mark is matte dark at 0.091444. Against a ground of luminance g the ghost composites to 0.16*0.881524 + 0.84g, so the two marks are equidistant from their ground when 0.1410438 - 0.16g = g - 0.091444, i.e. g = 0.2004205 with |delta| = 0.1089765 either way. Every member so far has drawn both marks against whatever darkness its host map happened to supply, and dark grounds favour the pale mark by a factor that nobody has measured. C_GROUND is that grey, and all three registers get it, because giving each account the ground that suits it would have destroyed the comparison.
dna.kin:
`removal` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the ruling is retention_corridor's. All six members use the word to stand in ONE account and forgo the other two; on this shell all three stand at once and that simultaneity IS the object. An axis whose every value demolishes two thirds of the exhibit is not a variation of it. The word is EXHIBITED instead - it names the artifact, it is engraved on the plinth under each register, and the value list is PRELOADED out of cantor_set.gd rather than retyped so the room cannot drift from the family it is about.

LAW 2 - NEST OR SIDE BY SIDE, answered from the members' CODE and not their prose. By EXTENT the three values NEST: cantor_set._spawn_removed draws nothing, then a box at 0.22 of the section, then a box at 1.0 of it, so the drawn set is empty, subset of scar, subset of ghost, and a scar cube is 0.22^3 = 1.065% of its own ghost's volume. By MATERIAL and by CLAIM they are PARALLEL: ghost is Color(0.86,0.88,0.96,0.16) unshaded with TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA and scar is Color(0.09,0.09,0.11) matte and opaque, and one says 'the part was here, this big' while the other says 'somebody cut here'. The case is therefore MIXED, and it decided the shape of the room: because ghost passes 84% of what is behind it, an all-at-once frame would show ghost's translucent shell WITH scar's dark core inside it and read as a single fourth value - three claims collapsed into one object. Side by side is the only arrangement in which the three stay three.

`subtraction` IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN WORD and no sibling declares it (checked across every registry file). Its VALUE LIST is the family's own census of cuts plus one import, derived and not invented: `third` is cantor_set, example_8_4_cantor_set_vr and its two aliases fractal_cantor_set and test_scene_3 - four of the six tokens; `cross` is menger_sponge; `figure` is recursive_chair; 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 and the list partitions the members exactly. `gasket` is sierpinski_triangle and is named as an IMPORT rather than smuggled in as a member, because that artifact answers this family's question under a rival word (`excision`: absence | ghost | rubble | cast | negative) and the room exists to hold the two vocabularies against one cut.

`tick` IS REFUSED AS A SECOND AXIS, and the arithmetic is the reason rather than taste - see dna.declines.
dna.declines:
`tick` REFUSED, and it was the obvious second axis: it is the family's own word (cantor_set, menger_sponge, example_8_4_cantor_set_vr and the two aliases all declare it) and depth is what a fractal of subtraction has. Two facts kill it.

FIRST, TWO OF THE FOUR VALUES CANNOT TAKE A RUNG. `figure` is recursive_chair, which subdivides ONCE and then deforms; three rungs there would be three byte-identical frames, which is the example_8_4 fault - rungs that exist in the enum and cannot be built. And `gasket` is an import whose own ladder belongs to a different word.

SECOND, THE ROOM CANNOT AFFORD THE RUNGS IT COULD BUILD, and the number is scale-free. Three non-overlapping registers make the shell about 5.4 cells wide whatever the cell is (see framing_why), so a cell is always about a fifth of the frame and at dna.framing 0.55 that is 126.09 px per metre. A Menger scar at rung 2 is 0.22 * CELL/9 = 0.024444 m = 3.08 px, inside the 1-3 px band law 4 exists because of, and no tightening of the framing moves it because tightening moves the whole shell with it. Rung 3 of `gasket` is 3.47 x 3.00 px for the same reason. Depth is therefore a CONSTANT chosen per value by the pixel width of that value's finest scar, recorded in the LEVELS table in the script with the number that fixed each one.

THIS IS A REAL COST AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE: menger_sponge ships max_iterations 2, and this room draws its cut at rung 1. `once` is a rung menger_sponge itself declares, so the room takes the family's ladder honestly rather than inventing a level - but the room is a WEAKER picture of a Menger sponge than menger_sponge is, and the reason is that it is photographing three of them.

THE SCAR MATERIAL IS LEFT LIT, on purpose, and this is the one asymmetry the room reports instead of fixing. Making it unshaded would pin it at luminance 0.091444 and make the computed-ground arithmetic exact under any light; it would also break the one property that keeps the six members photographing alike, since every one of them ships a lit scar and an unshaded ghost. The room reports the asymmetry rather than editing the family's recipe.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and this is worth stating rather than leaving blank. Both cantor_set and menger_sponge and recursive_chair needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before any axis of theirs was visible at all, because all three grow on a clock and a still at the harness's settle catches one falling bar or a half-built chair. This room has no clock, no RigidBody3D, no _process, no timer and no randf: _ready lays the finished row out in one frame and it never moves again. Nothing needs to be supplied.
dna.still_note:
READ THE Z-STACK BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER OFF THIS SHEET, because four separate things in this room were standing in front of marks and all four were found by arithmetic before any capture. The sweep camera stands at yaw 0.62, so with cy = cos(0.62) = 0.813878 and sy = sin(0.62) = 0.581039 a point lands at screen-x = cy*x - sy*z, and a thing of depth d eats sy*d of horizontal daylight while a gap of width g projects to only cy*g.

(1) THE REGISTERS WERE STANDING IN EACH OTHER'S LIGHT, and this rebuilt the shell. A CELL cube projects cy*CELL + sy*CELL = 1.394917 m of screen width. At the first PITCH of 1.14 the register centres were cy*1.14 = 0.927821 m apart, so consecutive cubes OVERLAPPED by 0.467096 m - 33.5% of a register's screen width. Of the middle register's 1 m2 footprint the part hidden by its right-hand neighbour is the triangle {screen-x >= 0.230396}, area 0.230650 m2 = 23.1%, including 70% of its right-hand face. Rasterised at the sweep's own 760 px the three cubes merged into ONE CONTINUOUS BLOCK and the row stopped being a row - and note what that would have looked like on the sheet: a large subject, four legible frames, and a perfectly respectable bite number, because the fault is identical at every value of the axis. PITCH must be at least 1.394917/cy = 1.714 * CELL; it is 1.75 * CELL, which leaves 0.029370 m = 3.70 px of daylight between registers and zero occlusion.

(2) THE PILASTERS. A 0.10 m fin standing 0.93 m deep casts a screen silhouette sy*0.93 + cy*0.10 = 0.621 m wide, six times its own thickness. With its front face at +0.30 that silhouette began at screen-x 0.248906 while a FLAT register's marks reach cy*0.5 = 0.406939, so the right 0.158033 m - 19.4% of the width of `third` and of `gasket` - stood behind a pilaster. FIN_FRONT is now -0.30 and the silhouette begins at 0.845690, clear of even the DEEP registers' 0.697459.

(3) THE LINTEL. The ray from a register's top-back corner (y 1.40, z -0.5) to the camera rises 0.25708/0.78652 = 0.326857 in y per unit z, crossing the soffit at y 1.50 when z = -0.194 and the head at y 1.60 when z = +0.112. With the lintel front at +0.30 that whole interval lay inside it: a wedge 0.1664 m deep at the back plane, 0.040800 m2 = 4.1% of a register's side profile. The lintel and cornice now stop at -0.30 with the fins, where the ray is 34.6 mm under the soffit as it leaves them.

(4) THE GROUND PANEL DOES NOT REACH THE LEFT END, and this one is REPORTED rather than fixed. The wall sits 0.605 m behind the marks, which shifts its silhouette sy*0.605 = 0.351529 m to screen-right, so its left edge lands at screen-x -1.825600 while the leftmost marks reach -2.121750. The unbacked wedge is 0.092733 m2 = 9.3% of that register's footprint at the two DEEP values and 0.7 px at the two flat ones. Closing it needs 0.432 m of extra wall on the LEFT ONLY, which is a camera-shaped shell and not a shell. It is tolerable because of WHERE it falls: the leftmost register is `gone`, the one account that draws neither a ghost nor a scar, so the computed ground - which exists to hold a pale mark and a dark one at equal distance - is untouched by it. The middle and right registers are backed edge to edge.

WHAT TO EXPECT ON THE SHEET. Subject share, rasterised: 26.08% (cross), 25.41% (third), 25.27% (gasket), 25.61% (figure) - comfortably over the ~6% floor, and the union subject box is 38.5% of frame area, so this is a WIDE subject in a square frame and not a small one. Instance counts are trivial: 20/7 cells at cross, 7/3 bars at third, 9/4 triangles at gasket, 16/11 cells at figure, drawn as five MultiMeshes per register set. Nothing here can trip the 16 s watchdog.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS EVERY VALUE OF THE AXIS, which for this artifact is the SHELL, because the shell is identical at all four values and encloses every register. Union box 5.41 x 1.64 x 1.145: x is SHELL_W + 2*CORNICE_OVER = 3*1.75 + 0.10 + 0.06; y runs 0 to SILL_Y+PANEL_H+LINTEL_H+CORNICE_H = 1.64; z runs from the cornice back at -0.645 to the plinth and CELL front at +0.50. Diagonal 5.767904, radius 2.883952.

THE RIG: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, dist = radius/tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 2.883952/0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.55 = 9.857241 m, so the visible frame is 2*PAD*radius*framing = 6.027450 m and a 760 px still is 126.0899 px per metre.

WHY 0.55 AND NOT 1.0: fit-by-DIAGONAL on a 5.41 x 1.64 body wastes most of a square frame. At yaw 0.62 the projected width is 5.41*cos(0.62) + 1.145*sin(0.62) = 4.403080 + 0.665290 = 5.068370 m, which is 84.1% of the 6.027450 m frame; the projected height is 2.632 m, 43.7% of it. Below about 0.50 the cornice starts to reach the frame edge.

EVERY MARK WAS GAUGED AGAINST 126.09 px/m BEFORE THE LEVELS WERE CHOSEN (law 4): cross scar 0.22*CELL/3 = 0.073333 m = 9.25 px; figure the same; gasket scar 0.22*0.25 = 0.055000 m = 6.93 px wide and 6.01 px tall; third scar 0.22*CANTOR_SEC_Y = 0.035200 m = 4.44 px, the thinnest mark in the room. The rungs that were REFUSED on this arithmetic are in dna.declines.

AND THE IN-REGISTER DAYLIGHT, because a gap that closes is the same fault as a mark that vanishes: `third` at two levels has a finest gap of CELL/9 = 0.111111 m projecting to 0.090431 m, against which a 0.06 deep section eats 0.034862 m and leaves 0.055569 m = 7.01 px - and cantor_set's own SQUARE 0.16 section would have eaten 0.092966 m and closed it completely, which is why the section here is anisotropic. `gasket` at two levels has a finest hole 0.25 wide projecting to 0.203470 m, against which sierpinski_triangle's own 0.14 extrusion would eat 0.081346 m; flat at 0.05 it eats 0.029052 m and leaves 0.174418 m = 21.99 px. `cross` at one level shows a face-centre recess 0.333333 wide projecting to 0.271293 m against a neighbouring cell eating 0.193680 m: 0.077613 m = 9.79 px still open.
dna.measured: PREDICTION SCORED, AND IT WAS THE WEAKEST OF THE FOUR IN THIS WAVE. Swept 2026-08-13, four frames, closest pair 5.86%. The registry predicted `cross` against `figure` as the closest at 1.1% of frame; measured, that pair is SECOND at 7.24% and the floor is `gasket` against `third` at 5.86% — which the prediction had ranked second, at 1.82%. So the two closest pairs were identified as a SET and their order swapped. The absolute numbers were low by about 6.5x, not the 1.5x the note allowed for, and the reason is stated there in advance: the Python rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading and no shadows, AO or antialiasing, so it systematically under-reports what a real render separates. The RANK was the claim and the rank was off by one place. Recorded because a prediction is only worth keeping if its misses are scored as plainly as its hits. Full order: gasket-third 5.86, cross-figure 7.24, figure-third 13.23, figure-gasket 13.63, cross-third 13.90, cross-gasket 14.01.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: `cross` against `figure`, at 15.7% focus and 1.1% frame. Both numbers are rasterised, not guessed - the four values were built in Python from the same constants the script uses, projected through the sweep's own camera at 760 px, and then put through artifact_dna_critic's exact currency: crop to the union subject box, neutralise each frame's own corner background, greyscale, resize 160x160, mean of |a-b| over the hottest 5%.

THE ARITHMETIC FOR WHY IT IS THAT PAIR. cross and figure are the same 1 m cube on the same 3x3x3 lattice at the same rung. cross deletes {4,10,12,13,14,16,22} and keeps 20; figure deletes {1,9,10,11,15,16,17,19,24,25,26} and keeps 16. They agree on 11 kept cells and on 2 deleted cells, so 13 of 27 cells - 48.1% - are drawn identically in every one of the three registers, and the GHOST register has the identical outer silhouette at both values, because 20+7 and 16+11 are both the whole cube. A third of the frame therefore differs only in the tan/pale distribution inside one unchanged outline. No other pair shares a lattice at all: `third` is 1D bars in rows and `gasket` is triangles.

FULL PREDICTED TABLE (frame / focus): cross-figure 1.08 / 15.67, third-gasket 1.82 / 22.63, cross-gasket 4.91 / 22.76, cross-third 4.49 / 22.84, gasket-figure 4.46 / 22.95, third-figure 4.36 / 23.37.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE PREDICTION AND WHAT IT WOULD MEAN. The rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading, no shadows, no ambient occlusion and no antialiasing, so the absolute numbers should not be trusted to better than a factor of about 1.5; the RANK is the claim. If the sweep returns cross-figure well ABOVE 15% while some other pair lands below it, the lattice argument is wrong somewhere and the cut functions should be diffed cell by cell. If any pair comes back under 3%, the room is not drawing what this entry says it draws - and the first thing to check is not the axis but the Z-STACK in still_note, because every one of the four faults listed there produced a picture that looked finished.
